newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Iraq says not signed oil contracts yet.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says not signed oil contracts yet.

text.p: Head of the Iraqi OPEC delegation Osama al-Hiti said on Wednesday that his country had yet to sign oil export contracts.
Al-Hiti was asked whether he would sell through spot sales and replied "No, it has to be six month contracts"
"We expect to sell of course to Europe, the U.S., South America and the Far East," he added.
"We are prepared to sign contracts as soon as we get the green light from the (OPEC) Secretary General," Hiti said. He added that exports would be in "a matter of weeks"
He said that Iraq would be be selling from Ceyhan in Turkey and Mina al Bakr.
Asked if would sell Iraq oil in 1996 he said "This is very hard now, we are waiting for the green light from the Secretary General."
He said Iraq would produce as much as they would be permitted to under the U.N. agreenment. They could produce as much as their OPEC allotment of 1.2 million barrels per day.
If he had to put an estimate on how much would be exporting, Hiti said it would be between 700,000 and 800,000 barrels per day.
He expected the reports back from inspectors Saybolt and Lloyds of London within a week from from the start of inspection , by very early December.
He said there would be no problems with the quality of the crude oil to be exported
